literal: In benignity exists the way of the world; the existence of those who do not have that is a burden to the earth.
translation: The smooth running of the world rests on the quality of benignity; the very existence of those who lack it is but a burden to the earth.
modern: உலக நடைமுறை கண்ணோட்டம் என்னும் பண்பில் தான் நிலைபெற்றுள்ளது; அப்பண்பு இல்லாதவர்களுடைய பிறப்பு இப்பூமிக்கு ஒரு பாரமே ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of kaṇṇōṭṭam (benignity, or a kindly, considerate outlook) for the sustenance of human society. The poet states that the orderly functioning and harmony of the world (ulakiyal) exist only because of this quality of kindness. For those who lack this gentle, sympathetic disposition (aḥtilār), their very existence (uṇmai) on this planet serves no positive purpose. Instead, they are described as a mere physical burden (poṟai) to the earth (nilakku), contributing nothing of value to the social fabric.
